text:
maria: Anyone else seeing a wave of preemptive evictions in eu-west1 this morning? small inference pods (0.25 GPU) are getting soft-evicted in bursts, downstream timeouts reported.
jon: yup, saw a spike around 07:12 UTC. kube-scheduler logs show a bunch of 'preempting for higher priority' churn. attaching a quick snippet.
jon: ```
NAMESPACE   NAME                       STATUS    NODE            RESTARTS   AGE
prod        inf-small-7b9c            Evicted   gpu-eu-3a-12    0          1h
prod        inf-small-4f2d            Evicted   gpu-eu-3b-11    0          55m
``` 
anika: we rolled pack-threshold change to 0.82 in the autoscaler canary last night to reduce idle GPUs. Could be related.
kai: also saw intermittent pod eviction loop + kubelet flaps on those nodes — network jitter between node <-> control-plane at the same time. CNI logs show bursty conntrack drops.
sre-bot: [alert] evictions_high: prod cluster eu-west1 — 78 evictions in last 15m. Pager duty: infra-oncall.
maria: if autoscaler is more aggressive, tiny pods lose the binpack lottery first. they don't have anti-affinity so they get squeezed.
jon: proposal: temporarily raise pack-threshold back to 0.9 for eu-west1 and roll back the canary. Also add a short-lived taint for new packed nodes to keep tiny pods from being preempted.
anika: note: raising threshold increases cost by ~4% (estimate) because we'll keep more nodes active. But avoids 5xxs for customers. tradeoff seems fine short-term.
kai: immediate mitigation we did: disabled the canary autoscaler change in eu-west1 and rebalance loop to drain fewer nodes at once.
maria: also adding a small PDB bump and soft-affinity for inf-small pods so they try to stay put during transient preempts.
jon: runbook steps I executed:
jon: ```
- rollback autoscaler canary in eu-west1
- kubectl cordon gpu-eu-3a-12 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- increase replicaset minReadySeconds for inf-small to 30s
``` 
anika: can we schedule a deeper postmortem after we stabilize? want to correlate pack-threshold, network jitter windows, and reclaim scoring algorithm.
kai: agree. also add a short metric to track 'tiny-pod preemption rate' so we can alarm before customer impact.
maria: thanks team — infra-oncall will keep watch for 2h and then hand off. action items: a) monitor evictions metric (kai), b) PM approve short-term cost increase (anika), c) postmortem doc (maria).
jon: I'll annotate the canary config in the repo so default is still 0.9 and canary lives in a branch until we get more data. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: [info] incident created: INC-2026-4124 — eu-west1 preemptive-evict-wave
maria: locking this thread to updates-only for now. Keep logs + evictions timestamps in the incident doc.
